text:
sam: Heads up — on NF4 canary we started seeing intermittent throughput drops with a ~2.3GB memory spike around 11:02 Pacific. Throughput down ~30% during incidents. :eyes:
infra-bot: [ALERT] host-gpu-copy-rate spike detected on pool-gamma at 2026-03-18T18:02:14Z. evict-rate=3.1x, mem-usage +2.3GB
maria: saw the same in canary metrics — p50 latency up ~90% for a subset of short-seq requests, tails worse. Correlated with batch sizes > 8 and seq <= 64.
devin: did a quick perf + pprof on the affected node. Flame shows `matmul_4bit_smallbatch` hot and a lot of memcpy in the caller. stack sample excerpt:
```
# samples 1200/1200
matmul_4bit_smallbatch  48%
memcpy_h2d_async       26%
scheduler_yield         6%
```
lucy: KV cache telemetry shows eviction rate spiking 3x during the window. Prefetch window length increases right before evictions; host->device copy bandwidth doubles. Looks like prefetch + kernel fallback causing duplicate copies.
sam: hypothesis: the new kernel-selection change (prefer_speed heuristics) is preferring a small-batch 4-bit kernel for certain seq length distributions, but when memory layout triggers fallback (FP4 path) we end up doing an extra host->device copy instead of inplace path. That double-copy plus scheduler contention causes the mem spike + throughput loss.
devin: repro steps I ran: `perf record -a -g -- sleep 30` + `go tool pprof -http` on the binary. Also ran: `./bench_runner --model gptx --seq 32 --microbatch 12 --quant nf4 --no-prefetch=false` — reproduces. Logs show repetitive: `copy_h2d start` / `copy_h2d start` within 5ms.
maria: I bisected to commit `2a3b4c` (kernel-selector: prefer_speed=true default). Reverting that flag locally returns baseline throughput and removes the mem bump. Not a permanent fix though.
lucy: mitigation ideas: 1) cap microbatch for this kernel variant to <=4; 2) short-circuit prefetch for seq<=64; 3) add a fast-path to avoid second copy when fallback happens (needs runtime change). Also add eviction-rate alert with lower threshold.
sam: immediate plan: hotfix canary by toggling prefer_speed=false and lowering prefetch window. @devin can you push the hotfix + collect end-to-end traces? :rocket:
devin: on it. I will open PR with the flag flip + a trace collection patch. Expect PR in ~90m. I'll include extended flamegraphs and a `--trace-kv` option to capture host-device ops.
ops-bot: [SCHEDULE] Patch rollout scheduled: 13:45 UTC -> 5% / 30% / 100% over 15m intervals.
sam: also let's add an automated perf microbenchmark in CI: sweep seq=(16,32,64,128,256) x microbatch=(1..16) for nf4/fp4 and check for >15% degradation relative to baseline.
maria: assigning follow-ups: devin (hotfix PR + traces), lucy (metrics + alert + prefetch flag config), sam (postmortem + perf test CI). I'll take notes for the postmortem. :memo:
sam: thanks — if anyone sees re-occurrence after the hotfix ping here immediately.
